d: Text filtering prevents users from seeing inappropriate language and blocks personally identifiable information.
h:
Applied to various sources and inputs, text filtering prevents users from seeing inappropriate language and personally identifiable information such as phone numbers. Roblox automatically filters common text outputs such as messages that have passed through in-game text chat, but you are responsible for filtering any displayed text that you don't have explicit control over.

Because filtering is crucial for a safe environment, Roblox actively moderates the content of games to make sure they meet community standards. If Roblox receives reports or automatically detects that your game doesn't apply text filtering, then the system removes the game until you add filtering.

Filter scenarios

Text can be gathered and/or displayed to users in a variety of scenarios, including:

  • A game that gathers users' text input through TextBox entries, a custom GUI with buttons such as a keyboard/keypad interface, or an interactive keyboard model in the 3D space.

  • A game that generates words from random characters and displays them to users, as there's a chance it will create inappropriate words.

  • A game that connects to an external web server to fetch content that is displayed in-game. Often you will not have control over the content of the external site and a third party can edit the information.

  • A game that stores text such as users' pet names using data stores, where the stored text might include inappropriate words that should be filtered when retrieving them.

Filtering process

TextService:FilterStringAsync() filters in-game text by taking a string of text and the UserId of the user who created the text as input. It returns a TextFilterResult object which has two additional methods that you can call in different scenarios:

  • TextFilterResult:GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync() for filtering text visible to all users in a game, such as for a dialog that lets a user write a message on a sign that's visible to all users on the server.
  • TextFilterResult:GetNonChatStringForUserAsync() to display filtered text for one specific user, based on age and other details.

In the context of TextBox input, the following example gathers input on the FocusLost event and sends it to the server through a RemoteEvent. On the server, it is filtered first through FilterStringAsync() and then GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync() with the intention that the text will be displayed to all users on a server‑side object such as a SurfaceGui in the 3D world.

Do not filter text in real time "per character entered" into a TextBox, as doing so yields for text that's only visible to the user typing it. Instead, filter the entered text after the user submits it.

Filtering Text Input - Client Script

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local textBox = script.Parent
textBox.ClearTextOnFocus = false
textBox.PlaceholderText = "..."
textBox.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
textBox.TextScaled = true

-- RemoteEvent to send text input to server for filtering
local inputRemoteEvent = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("InputRemoteEvent")

-- Event handler for focus lost and enter being pressed
local function onFocusLost(enterPressed, inputObject)
    if enterPressed then
        print("SUBMITTED:", textBox.Text)
        if inputRemoteEvent then
            inputRemoteEvent:FireServer(textBox.Text)
        end
    end
end

textBox.FocusLost:Connect(onFocusLost)

Filtering Text Input - Server Script

local TextService = game:GetService("TextService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

-- RemoteEvent to receive text input from client for filtering
local inputRemoteEvent = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("InputRemoteEvent")

local function getFilterResult(text, fromUserId)
    local filterResult
    local success, errorMessage = pcall(function()
        filterResult = TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, fromUserId)
    end)

    if success then
        return filterResult
    else
        warn("Error generating TextFilterResult:", errorMessage)
    end
end

-- Fired when client submits input from the TextBox
local function onInputReceived(player, text)
    if text ~= "" then
        local filterResult = getFilterResult(text, player.UserId)
        if filterResult then
            local success, filteredText = pcall(function()
                return filterResult:GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync()
            end)

            if success then
                print("FILTERED:", filteredText)
            else
                warn("Error filtering text!")
            end
        end
    end
end

inputRemoteEvent.OnServerEvent:Connect(onInputReceived)

kid.simple: Text filtering hides bad words and private info, like phone numbers, before other players see them. Roblox already filters normal chat for you, but any other text players type or your game makes, like a pet name or a message on a sign, is your job to filter. This is a big deal: if Roblox finds that your game shows unfiltered text, it can take your game down until you fix it. The page shows how to send text to the server and filter it with `TextService`.
kid.analogy: It is like a teacher checking notes before they get pinned on the class bulletin board. Anything that goes up for everyone to see has to pass the check first.
keyPoints: You must filter any displayed text you do not fully control, like player typing, random word generators, text from outside websites, or names saved in data stores.
Roblox chat is filtered for you. Your own text boxes and signs are not.
On the server, call `TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, userId)` with the text and the `UserId` of the player who wrote it. It gives back a `TextFilterResult`.
Use `GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync()` for text everyone will see, like a sign on the server.
Use `GetNonChatStringForUserAsync()` when the text is shown to just one specific player.
Filter after the player submits (for example, presses Enter), not on every letter they type.
Wrap the filter calls in `pcall` because they can fail, and handle the error.

terms.text filtering: Roblox's system that replaces bad words or private info with hashtags before others see it.
terms.personally identifiable information: Info that could find a real person, like a phone number, address, or full name.
terms.UserId: The unique number Roblox gives each account. The filter needs the writer's UserId to filter correctly.
terms.TextFilterResult: The object you get back from `FilterStringAsync`. You call one of its methods to get the cleaned-up text.
terms.broadcast: Show to everyone in the server, like a public sign.
terms.RemoteEvent: A messenger that sends info between a player's device (client) and the server. Here it carries the typed text to the server.
terms.client: The player's own device. LocalScripts run here.
terms.server: Roblox's computer running the game for everyone. Filtering must happen here.
terms.yield: Pause and wait for something to finish. Filter functions yield while Roblox checks the text.
terms.pcall: A safe way to call a function. If the function errors, the script keeps running and tells you it failed instead of crashing.
terms.FocusLost: An event on a `TextBox` that fires when the player stops typing in it, for example by pressing Enter or clicking away.

example.title: Filter text a player types for a public sign
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService (plus a RemoteEvent named InputRemoteEvent in ReplicatedStorage, and a LocalScript in the TextBox that fires it)
example.code:
local TextService = game:GetService("TextService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local inputRemoteEvent = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("InputRemoteEvent")

local function onInputReceived(player, text)
	-- Ignore empty or non-text input
	if typeof(text) ~= "string" or text == "" then
		return
	end

	-- Step 1: ask Roblox to check the text from this player
	local ok, filterResult = pcall(function()
		return TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, player.UserId)
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("Could not filter text:", filterResult)
		return
	end

	-- Step 2: get the version that is safe for everyone to see
	local ok2, filteredText = pcall(function()
		return filterResult:GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync()
	end)
	if ok2 then
		print("FILTERED:", filteredText) -- show this on your sign
	else
		warn("Error filtering text!")
	end
end

inputRemoteEvent.OnServerEvent:Connect(onInputReceived)
explain: The LocalScript in the TextBox sends the typed text with `FireServer` when the player presses Enter.
On the server, `OnServerEvent` gives us the player who sent it and the text.
We skip empty text or anything that is not a string.
`FilterStringAsync` checks the text, using the sender's `UserId`. We wrap it in `pcall` in case it fails.
`GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync` returns text that is safe for everyone, which you can then put on a sign or SurfaceGui.

watchOut: Showing player text without filtering it. Roblox can remove your game until you add filtering.
Filtering on the client. Filtering must be done on the server, so send the text with a RemoteEvent.
Filtering every keystroke. Wait until the player submits, then filter once.
Using the broadcast method for text only one player sees, or the other way around. Pick broadcast for everyone, `ForUser` for one person.
Not using `pcall`. The filter can fail, and without `pcall` your script errors out.
